newsitem.title: INDIA: Thirty-seven countries to attend Goa oil talks.
newsitem.headline: Thirty-seven countries to attend Goa oil talks.

text.p: Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Nuaimi will not attend energy talks starting here on Saturday designed to foster cooperation between oil producers and consumers, a spokeswoman for host India said.

But Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh is still expected to travel to Goa for the fifth in a series of international conferences convened since the 1990-1991 Gulf War. The conference will be opened on Friday by Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil producer and exporter, will be represented by Ministry Director Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman.
OPEC ministers from Indonesia, Nigeria, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela are also expected to attend.
Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov, Norway's new Energy Minister Grete Faremo and Egyptian Petroleum Minister Hamdi el-Banbi will represent major non-OPEC oil producers.
Other OPEC members, including Kuwait and Iraq, are sending oil ministry officials.
Ministerial representation from consumer countries is restricted to India, Portugal and South Africa. Major consumers the United States, Germany, Japan and France are sending ministry officials.
Representatives from 37 countries are scheduled to arrive in Goa over the next two days, including 16 at ministerial level, from an original list of 46 expected attendees.
OPEC, the International Energy Agency, the European Commission and the Gulf Cooperation Council will also send representatives.
Presentations and discussions on Saturday and Sunday will target the growing energy needs of emerging economies and the implications for world energy trade and the environment.
